programmes.title: Cloud Computing & DevOps
programmes.skills: Linux, networking, Docker, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, reliability
programmes.goal: Deploy and operate a reproducible, secure cloud application.
programmes.audience: Junior developers and IT support learners. Basic Git and command-line familiarity recommended; use the coding programme first if needed.
modules: Cloud Computing Fundamentals
Compare service models and select a cost-aware deployment architecture.
Design a cloud architecture for a fictional application, with cost assumptions and a teardown checklist.
Linux and Networking
Explain processes, permissions, DNS, HTTP and network boundaries.
Set up a local Linux lab, document least-privilege permissions and troubleshoot a local service.
Containers and Docker
Build a reproducible, non-root container and verify its behaviour.
Containerise a sample web application, add health checks and document image dependencies.
CI/CD and GitHub Actions
Design a gated pipeline for repeatable testing and deployment.
Create a workflow that tests, builds and validates a sample application without exposing credentials.
Infrastructure as Code
Describe declarative infrastructure, review changes and manage state safely.
Create a reviewed local or sandbox infrastructure plan with variables, cost limits and cleanup instructions.
Cloud Security and Reliability
Define service indicators, recovery objectives, monitoring and security controls.
Run a controlled failure exercise, document recovery and propose an alerting and access policy.
programmes.cap: Deploy a sample application using containers and a gated CI/CD pipeline, infrastructure plan, monitoring, threat model, rollback and cost controls.
sample: A new application version fails its health check after deployment.
What should the pipeline do?
Ignore the health check
Stop or roll back the release using the documented recovery procedure
Remove all monitoring
A failed health check should prevent an unhealthy release from becoming the normal production version. Follow the tested rollback or recovery procedure.

programmes.title: Financial Accounting & Digital Bookkeeping
programmes.skills: Double-entry, journals, ledgers, reconciliation, payroll concepts, financial statements
programmes.goal: Maintain accurate business books and interpret basic financial reports.
programmes.audience: Students, administrative staff, entrepreneurs and aspiring bookkeepers. Basic arithmetic and spreadsheet access recommended.
modules: Accounting Fundamentals
Classify assets, liabilities, equity, income and expenses using the accounting equation.
Analyse ten fictional business transactions and explain their effect on the accounting equation.
Journals, Ledgers and Trial Balance
Post double-entry transactions and reconcile a trial balance.
Prepare journals, ledgers and an adjusted trial balance from a synthetic transaction set.
Digital Bookkeeping Systems
Design a chart of accounts, source-document register and audit trail.
Create a simulated bookkeeping file with customer and supplier records, reference numbers and posting controls.
Bank Reconciliation and Financial Controls
Reconcile cashbook and bank balances and identify exceptions.
Prepare a bank reconciliation with outstanding items, corrections and documented approval.
Payroll and Tax Administration
Explain gross-to-net payroll, record controls and statutory obligations without assuming fixed tax rates.
Prepare an illustrative payroll register using explicitly provided hypothetical deductions; identify official sources for current statutory rates.
Financial Statements and Analysis
Prepare basic financial statements from adjusted records and interpret key ratios.
Produce an income statement, statement of financial position and management commentary with reconciled balances.
programmes.cap: Complete a fictional month-end bookkeeping cycle, including reconciled journals, ledger, trial balance, payroll simulation, financial statements and a control report.
sample: A business receives R5,000 cash from a customer who previously owed it R5,000.
Which accounts change?
Cash increases and accounts receivable decreases
Revenue increases again
Cash decreases and expenses increase
Debit cash and credit accounts receivable. The collection does not create revenue a second time.

programmes.title: Digital Marketing & E-commerce
programmes.skills: Marketing strategy, content, SEO, advertising, conversion, e-commerce
programmes.goal: Plan and evaluate an ethical digital customer-acquisition strategy.
programmes.audience: Small-business owners, aspiring marketers and freelancers. No advertising spend required.
modules: Marketing Fundamentals
Identify audiences, customer needs and measurable marketing objectives.
Create a target audience profile, value proposition and campaign objective.
Social Media and Content Strategy
Plan audience-relevant content and measure engagement responsibly.
Create a two-week content calendar with creative briefs, accessibility checks and consent considerations.
SEO and Search Marketing
Explain search intent, crawlability, on-page SEO and measurement.
Audit a fictional landing page and create an additive SEO improvement plan.
Paid Advertising and Analytics
Calculate campaign metrics, compare hypotheses and respect budget limits.
Evaluate a synthetic campaign dataset and propose a budget allocation without launching ads.
E-commerce Operations and Conversion
Map checkout, fulfilment, returns and conversion barriers.
Design a store journey, test checklist and privacy-conscious measurement plan.
programmes.cap: Build a digital campaign portfolio for a fictional online store, including SEO audit, content calendar, simulated advertising analysis, conversion plan and reporting dashboard.
sample: A campaign receives 2,000 impressions and 100 clicks.
What is its click-through rate?
CTR = clicks ÷ impressions × 100 = 100 ÷ 2,000 × 100 = 5%. CTR alone does not prove profitability.

programmes.title: Project Management & Agile Delivery
programmes.skills: Scope, schedules, budgets, Scrum, risks, stakeholders, quality
programmes.goal: Plan, deliver and evaluate a project using appropriate delivery methods.
programmes.audience: Aspiring project coordinators, team leaders and business students.
modules: Project Management Fundamentals
Define objectives, scope, deliverables, roles and success criteria.
Produce a project charter and stakeholder register for a fictional project.
Planning, Scheduling and Budgeting
Estimate effort, dependencies, milestones and costs.
Build a schedule, dependency map and baseline budget with contingency assumptions.
Agile and Scrum
Explain iterative delivery and appropriate Scrum accountabilities and events.
Create a prioritised backlog, sprint goal and simulated sprint review.
Risk and Stakeholder Management
Assess risks, plan responses and communicate changes.
Maintain a risk register, communications matrix and approved change request.
Project Delivery and Quality Assurance
Verify deliverables, manage acceptance and close a project.
Create a quality checklist, acceptance report, lessons learned and handover package.
programmes.cap: Manage a simulated product launch from charter to closure, including plan, budget, backlog, risk register, status reports and acceptance evidence.
sample: A stakeholder requests an extra feature after scope is agreed.
What is the best next step?
Add it without informing the team
Assess impact and follow the agreed change process
Cancel the project
Evaluate impact on scope, cost, schedule and quality, then obtain the appropriate decision before changing the baseline.

programmes.title: Advanced AI Automation & Agents
programmes.skills: LLM APIs, structured outputs, RAG, MCP, agents, evaluation, deployment
programmes.goal: Build constrained, testable AI automation systems with human oversight.
programmes.audience: Developers with basic Python or JavaScript, APIs and Git experience. AI literacy and coding foundations recommended.
modules: Applied Large Language Models
Select models and explain context, latency, cost and reliability trade-offs.
Create a model comparison and evaluation matrix using synthetic tasks and explicit budgets.
AI APIs and Structured Outputs
Validate structured responses, handle errors and protect credentials.
Implement a local mock API client with schema validation, retry limits and test cases.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation
Design document retrieval, citations, abstention and evaluation.
Build a small local retrieval system using an approved fictional corpus and labelled test questions.
Agent Architecture and MCP
Describe tool contracts, trust boundaries and explicit permissions.
Implement a read-only tool interface with allowlisted operations and malicious-input tests.
Multi-Agent Workflow Automation
Coordinate bounded steps, state and human approvals.
Design a workflow with deterministic handoffs, timeouts, an audit log and simulated approvals.
AI Security, Evaluation and Deployment
Evaluate prompt injection, unsafe tool calls, privacy and operational failure.
Run an evaluation suite and document mitigations, cost limits, deployment and rollback.
programmes.cap: Build a constrained research or administrative agent using synthetic data, citations, typed tool contracts, human approval, security tests and reproducible deployment.
sample: An agent retrieves a document containing instructions to send private files elsewhere.
How should the system treat those instructions?
As authorised commands
As untrusted document content that cannot grant permissions
As a reason to expose all credentials
Retrieved content is data, not authority. Tool permissions and human approvals must be enforced independently of model-generated instructions.

programmes.title: CRM, Sales & Customer Success
programmes.skills: Sales discovery, CRM, pipeline, ethical prospecting, negotiation, retention
programmes.goal: Manage a customer pipeline and improve service outcomes using structured records.
programmes.audience: Sales representatives, entrepreneurs, customer support staff and job seekers.
modules: Professional Selling
Conduct needs discovery and map solutions to customer requirements.
Create a discovery script, qualification notes and value-based proposal.
CRM Systems and Pipeline Management
Define lifecycle stages, ownership, data quality and pipeline metrics.
Build a fictional CRM dataset with stage definitions, next actions and forecast assumptions.
Customer Acquisition and Lead Generation
Plan permission-aware prospecting and measure acquisition.
Create a synthetic lead list and compliant outreach sequence with opt-out handling; no live bulk messaging.
Negotiation and Communication
Prepare an ethical negotiation with clear objectives and boundaries.
Role-play a client negotiation and document agreed next steps and concessions.
Customer Retention and Success
Track onboarding, customer health, feedback and renewal risks.
Create a customer success plan, health-score rationale and escalation workflow.
programmes.cap: Develop a complete simulated customer lifecycle portfolio from discovery to renewal, including CRM records, pipeline dashboard, proposal, onboarding and retention plan.
sample: A prospect asks not to receive further marketing messages.
What should happen?
Add them to another campaign
Respect the request and update the suppression record
Delete the request and continue contacting them
Respect the opt-out, record it in the appropriate suppression workflow and follow applicable privacy and marketing requirements.
